description: The tagged result every menger process the scene agent runs prints on stdout when it ends at once (SceneValidator, run-sandboxed.sh, run-render-window.sh, menger-app's render-lock refusal), and the exit code that goes with each tag. Owned by menger (review 2026-10-14, menger#82/#100); ProcessContractSuite holds every producer to it; the agent keeps a copy in reference/ and holds its parser to it. A wall-clock timeout of the sandbox wrapper (exit 124) prints nothing; the validator's own limit (100 s, below the wrapper's 120 s) is a `refused` result.
meaningOfOk: SceneValidator's `ok` (exit 0) means the scene compiled, loaded and passed every check, and that the validator itself said so, not the scene: the scene's code runs in a worker process, and the result is the line of the worker's output that carries a secret the scene never sees. A scene that prints a result of its own, ends its process (System.exit, Runtime.halt) or keeps it alive with a thread cannot change the verdict; one that ends the validation before a result is `refused` (exit 2), never `ok`. What remains: scene code runs with the worker's privileges, so a scene that reads the secret out of the worker's memory (a heap dump through the management interface, for example) can still forge the line. The container is the security boundary; `ok` holds against a scene that is wrong, greedy or casually hostile, not against every adversary (menger#137).

windowEvents.description: What the interactive window writes, one JSON object per line, to <scene file>.events.jsonl next to the scene it watches. Replaces reading the window's log lines (review 2026-10-14, menger#82). Scene code runs in the same process and could write one too: an event is a report, not proof.
